rationale: All 6 candidates are direct matches (trait_reported/trait_efo and phenotyping_reported all indicate abdominal aortic aneurysm; one is explicitly prevalent AAA but still aligned). Best-supported is PGS000753 because it is from a disease-focused AAA genetics study (Circulation; MVP/MAYO-VDB), reports a PRS-comparable effect size (OR per SD 1.37, 95% CI 1.30–1.44) with basic covariates (age, sex, PCs), and avoids reliance on full-model AUROC as a proxy for PRS performance (its AUC/R2 are not reported). Runners-up are the two Nat Genet meta-analysis PRS-CS models (PGS003972/PGS003973) due to strong disease-focused multi-cohort development and direct AAA endpoint; however, their reported discrimination is only via full-model AUROC/C-index (0.69 and 0.882) with no PGS-only metrics, and the very high C-index for PGS003973 is likely covariate-driven (age/age^2/sex), limiting comparability. Overall outcome is DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL because across the pool, PRS-only AUC is absent and the available metrics are heterogeneous (effect size vs partial-r vs covariate-heavy full-model AUROC), leaving meaningful uncertainty in ranking. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

All four candidates are direct matches to the target concept (alcohol dependence/AUD): PGS002738 and PGS002739 map to trait_efo="alcohol dependence" with phenotyping_reported="Alcohol use disorder"; PGS000201/PGS000202 map to "alcohol dependence measurement" but their phenotyping_reported is also AUD DSM-5 criteria count. PGS002738 is best supported because it has the most endpoint-faithful labeling (trait_reported="Alcohol use disorder", trait_efo="alcohol dependence") and provides a clear discriminative effect size (OR top 10% vs rest = 1.96, 95% CI 1.54–2.51) in a reasonably sized EUR evaluation (n=7,900), with development cohorts including MVP and UKB. The main limitation is that none of the candidates report PRS-only AUC/R2, and PGS002738 has covariates listed as Unknown, reducing comparability and keeping confidence below High. Runners-up: PGS000201 and PGS000202 are from the same publication family with the same AUD DSM-5 criteria endpoint and explicit incremental ΔR²; PGS000201 ranks above PGS000202 due to higher ΔR² (0.01192 vs 0.00456), larger validation size (7,599 vs 1,251), and stronger beta (0.099 vs 0.043). PGS002739 is deprioritized as a runner-up despite being a direct AUD score because it is evaluated only in African American/Afro-Caribbean ancestry (EVAL: AFR 100%), making it less broadly supported as a general direct-match choice in this context compared with the EUR-evaluated alternatives.
